mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in FEDFUNDS and UNRATE above 5.0% signal aggressive monetary tightening during labor market weakness, suppressing equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp and UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1200.0 thousand units during housing market recovery phases signal stronger consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1200.0, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 105.0 index signals robust manufacturing expansion that boosts corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 105.0, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained non-farm payroll growth above 150,000 jobs per month signals strengthening labor markets that increase consumer spending and corporate revenue, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 150,000, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent housing starts above 1200.0 thousand units and retail sales above 460,000 million dollars signal strong consumer demand that boosts corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 1200.0 and RSAFS > 460000.0, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), a federal funds rate increase signals aggressive monetary tightening that suppresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25pp, or Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows.
